Missing Person Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 July 2024. Immediate-search window shortened from 30 to 15 minutes.

1. Immediate search

A 15-minute site and immediate-grounds search is conducted (shortened from the previous 30 minutes)
before escalating further.

2. Police contact

If not found after the immediate search, police are called on 101 (or 999 if there is immediate risk).

Immediate response

Staff confirm the person is not elsewhere on site, note the last verified sighting, clothing, mobility,
communication needs and likely destinations, and preserve relevant CCTV or access records. The
registered manager assesses immediate vulnerability and calls emergency services without delay where
risk is high; local searching never postpones a necessary police report.

Search and communication

The search is coordinated, logged and allocated so unsafe duplication and unsearched areas are visible.
Staff maintain safe staffing for residents who remain on site. Family, commissioners and safeguarding
contacts are informed according to the person's plan and the circumstances, while public communication
and photographs are released only through the police-led or otherwise authorised route.

Return and learning

On return, immediate welfare and medical needs are assessed before a calm account is sought. The care
plan, risk assessment and known triggers are reviewed with the person and relevant representatives. The
incident record includes timings, decisions, notifications and search activity, and repeated episodes or
control failures are escalated for safeguarding and service-level review.

Purpose and scope

This FAQ explains how a staff member can check their own training record and request a refresher. It applies to every member of staff.

Policy statement

Every staff member can see their own current training status at any time, supporting them to stay on top of an upcoming refresher rather than being caught out by an unexpected lapse.

Definitions

**Mandatory Training Matrix** the central record of every staff member's required training and its expiry date. **Lapsed training** training that has passed its expiry date without a refresher being completed. **Refresher** the shorter, periodic training update required to keep a qualification current.

1. Check current training status at any time through the staff portal, which reflects the Mandatory Training Matrix.
2. Receive an automated reminder 6 weeks before a mandatory training item expires.
3. Book a refresher session directly through the staff portal once reminded.
4. Escalate to the registered manager if a refresher session cannot be booked before the expiry date approaches closely.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This FAQ works alongside the Mandatory Training Matrix itself (the underlying record this FAQ helps staff navigate) and the specific policy area a lapsed training item relates to, such as safeguarding or medication competency.

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the reminder cycle. A staff member's manual handling refresher is due in six weeks. Supersedes the version effective 1 May 2025. Adds a lost-item tracking log following recurring family
concern about missing clothing, and a dedicated laundering protocol for reusable PPE items.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how a resident's clothing and site linen, and reusable PPE, is laundered at
Alderbridge Care Group. It applies to every site's laundry operation.

Policy statement

A resident's own clothing is laundered separately within the barrier system, with a new lost-item tracking
log addressing recurring family concern about missing clothing, and reusable PPE now follows its own
dedicated laundering protocol distinct from resident clothing and general linen.

Definitions

**Barrier laundry system** the one-way dirty-to-clean flow protecting against cross-contamination.
**Lost-item tracking log** the new log, introduced in this version, recording every reported missing clothing
item and its resolution. **Reusable PPE** a washable apron or similar item, now laundered under its own
dedicated protocol rather than alongside general site linen.

Roles and responsibilities

**Laundry staff** follow the barrier system, complete the new lost-item tracking log entry for a reported
missing item, and follow the new dedicated reusable PPE protocol. **Care staff** identify and bag soiled
linen and reusable PPE separately for correct handling. **The registered manager** reviews the lost-item
tracking log monthly for a recurring pattern.

1. Follow the barrier system's one-way dirty-to-clean flow.

2. Label every resident's clothing clearly on admission.

3. Launder a resident's own clothing separately from another resident's items and from site linen.

4. Wash soiled linen at 65 degrees Celsius within the barrier system.

5. Log a reported missing clothing item in the new lost-item tracking log the same day it is reported,
including a description and last known laundry batch; this is a new requirement introduced in this version.

Learning from Deaths Policy

*Supersedes the version effective 1 February 2025. Sections reordered to lead with family communication before the review process; no requirement changed.*

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group communicates with a resident's family following their death, and how the death is reviewed to identify any genuine learning. It applies to every site.

Policy statement

Every family is thanked for their trust and invited to share feedback on the care provided, and every death is briefly reviewed at the next Quality Committee to identify any learning, without implying any death was unexpected or poorly managed.

Definitions

**Learning from deaths review** the brief, routine review conducted for every resident death, distinct from a fuller investigation triggered by a specific concern. **Quality Committee** the body that receives the review and any theme identified across multiple reviews over time.

Roles and responsibilities

**A nominated staff member** contacts the family sensitively to thank them and, where appropriate, invite feedback. **The registered manager** prepares a brief summary for the Quality Committee following every death. **The Quality Committee** identifies any genuine, recurring learning theme across reviews.

1. Contact the family, at a sensitive and appropriate time, to thank them for their trust in Alderbridge's care.
2. Invite the family to share feedback on the care provided, where this feels appropriate given their circumstances, without pressuring them to respond.
3. Prepare a brief review summary for every resident death, presented at the next Quality Committee meeting.
4. Identify whether the review suggests any genuine learning, distinct from the routine, expected nature of end of life care generally.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a death raises a specific concern beyond the routine review (for example, an unexpected circumstance), this is escalated to a fuller investigation under the Incident Reporting Policy and, where relevant, the Duty of Candour Guidance, rather than being addressed only through the routine Quality Committee review.

Purpose and scope

Policy statement

A resident's own clothing is laundered separately within the barrier system, with a new lost-item tracking
log addressing recurring family concern about missing clothing, and reusable PPE now follows its own
dedicated laundering protocol distinct from resident clothing and general linen.

Definitions

dedicated protocol rather than alongside general site linen.

missing item, and follow the new dedicated reusable PPE protocol. **Care staff** identify and bag soiled
linen and reusable PPE separately for correct handling. **The registered manager** reviews the lost-item
tracking log monthly for a recurring pattern.

Policy statement

Every family is thanked for their trust and invited to share feedback on the care provided, and every death is briefly reviewed at the next Quality Committee to identify any learning, without implying any death was unexpected or poorly managed.

Definitions

**Learning from deaths review** the brief, routine review conducted for every resident death, distinct from a fuller investigation triggered by a specific concern. **Quality Committee** the body that receives the review and any theme identified across multiple reviews over time.

They call the South West on-call number directly, reaching a manager who knows the region's specific context, sites and relationships well, a difference from the previous version where the answering manager might have had no prior familiarity with that region at all.

They lock the screen first, even though they expect to be back within a minute, since a brief absence is exactly the kind of moment an unlocked screen creates unnecessary risk.

Frequently asked questions

**Can a password manager be used to store an Alderbridge system password?** Yes, using the Alderbridge-approved password manager specifically; a personal, unapproved tool is not used for this purpose. **What happens if a staff member suspects their account has been accessed by someone else?** They contact IT immediately, who resets access and investigates, following the Cyber Incident Response Plan if warranted.

Training and competency

All staff receive password and account security guidance at induction, refreshed annually alongside wider cyber awareness training.

Where a system offers multi-factor authentication, this is enabled and used rather than relying on a password alone, since a password can be guessed or exposed in a way a second, device-based factor makes much harder for an attacker to bypass.

A personal, strong password kept confidential protects far more than the individual account it belongs to, and this guidance exists to make that simple habit consistent across every system.

Missing Person Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 July 2024. Immediate-search window shortened from 30 to 15 minutes.

1. Immediate search

A 15-minute site and immediate-grounds search is conducted (shortened from the previous 30 minutes)
before escalating further.

2. Police contact

If not found after the immediate search, police are called on 101 (or 999 if there is immediate risk).

Immediate response

Staff confirm the person is not elsewhere on site, note the last verified sighting, clothing, mobility,
communication needs and likely destinations, and preserve relevant CCTV or access records. The
registered manager assesses immediate vulnerability and calls emergency services without delay where
risk is high; local searching never postpones a necessary police report.

Search and communication

The search is coordinated, logged and allocated so unsafe duplication and unsearched areas are visible.
Staff maintain safe staffing for residents who remain on site. Family, commissioners and safeguarding
contacts are informed according to the person's plan and the circumstances, while public communication
and photographs are released only through the police-led or otherwise authorised route.

Return and learning

On return, immediate welfare and medical needs are assessed before a calm account is sought. The care
plan, risk assessment and known triggers are reviewed with the person and relevant representatives. The
incident record includes timings, decisions, notifications and search activity, and repeated episodes or
control failures are escalated for safeguarding and service-level review.
